evidence: createApp registers Express routes (app.post/app.get/app.patch): transport responsibility, which fits infrastructure
Each route hands the work to service.addProduct / placeOrder / listOrders / progressOrder / cancelOrder, so no business logic is written inline
isRecord and the checks against fulfilmentStates only validate the shape of incoming requests, not transition rules
The error middleware maps DomainError codes to 404/409/400/500: translating errors into HTTP responses is transport work
orderView/productView are response mappers for the presentation boundary
The default parameter builds OrderService with in-memory repositories, which is composition-root wiring and fits infrastructure
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file passes: everything it does belongs in an infrastructure (transport) adapter. It sets up Express routes and parses JSON. It checks the shape of incoming requests and maps domain objects to response views. It also maps DomainError codes to HTTP status codes and wires in default dependencies. Every business operation (addProduct, placeOrder, listOrders, progressOrder, cancelOrder) is handed to OrderService, so stock and order-state rules are not reimplemented here. The query/body checks against fulfilmentStates only validate request input. They do not decide which state transitions are allowed. Throwing DomainError for bad input is a small stylistic coupling, not a business rule placed in the wrong layer.
